approach.method_basis: The Parent evolves a task-local population of accepted molecular graphs. It keeps up to 64 survivors ordered by observed score and insertion order, independently chooses breeding parents through three preferred score bands, and generates fresh molecules by connected-fragment crossover and local atom/bond edits, including short mutation walks. Direct aromatic carbon/nitrogen positional exchange is disabled. A Gaussian process trained on the complete accepted-score archive uses counts of local molecular environments and generalized Tanimoto similarity; correlated posterior draws select the next announced batch from a full surplus pool. Accepted offspring update both the model archive and the breeding population.
approach.novelty: Introduce randomly permuted systematic blocks for first-parent requests. Each prospective block keeps the Parent's exact rank preference and positive support, but its counts stay close to their expected allocation before the records are consumed in random order. Block length is the existing fresh-pool target. Earlier siblings changed the eligible support, marginal parent weights, survivor retention or proposal lifetime; this experiment changes only dependence among first-parent draws and keeps crossover-partner selection inherited. The hypothesis is that limiting accidental allocation clumps can improve the supply of useful offspring while retaining strong parents. The guarantee concerns prospective complete blocks; validity-dependent stopping can bias consumed prefixes, and improved endpoints remain an untested prediction.

observed_bottleneck: The code Parent n-62daf219c70a uses independent first-parent draws, so finite generation effort can repeatedly allocate more or fewer requests to an accepted parent than its supported rank preference implies. The actual three Parent summary.json and run.log files are complete: macro mean 0.5956696497334577, population SD 0.02659287062806747, with all fifteen task runs successful. A read-only reconstruction of every Parent task log, excluding duplicate breed/outcome=emitted receipts, finds 75,961 first-parent and 34,334 second-parent requests, 435 full pools, and 161 to 197 first requests per suggestion (mean 174.62298850574712). Grouping only real first requests into consecutive complete windows of the inherited pool target gives 435 windows; every window has at least one parent count outside floor(B*q_i)..ceil(B*q_i), with mean maximum absolute count deviation 6.269272030651341. Actual first-parent support averages 24.32183908045977 identities per suggestion versus 29 identities in positive q support. The remaining real request tails contain 1 to 37 requests, mean 14.622988505747127. These are opportunity measurements, not evidence that repetition caused poor scores or that a stopped systematic prefix will help. The audit is .slots/L01-resume-20260928/r22-slot1/parent_plan_audit.json and contains all session/batch counts and source hashes. n-f30747ffdbf8 preserves original support while removing unequal rank weights and loses 0.05700288256234002 in paired macro mean, with eleven declining and four improving endpoints. Its parent wins rise 629 to 936 against weaker best-parent references, while absolute offspring scores and incumbent advances fall. n-a56491c332aa removes support restriction and weights together, losing 0.04599801243765703 with thirteen declining and two improving endpoints. Historical n-69c038cb49ac (c-19e5b43df7) and n-030a6ccbba7c (c-5b78099161), both on the older n-fc2c108a5253 Parent/profile, alter within-band marginals and lose 0.020256296737091634 and 0.02157946287432137 despite broader core use or more local gains. n-2e9e08198747 makes protected records breed under a joint retention/uniform-live intervention yet loses 0.06516141262576135, with twelve declining and three improving endpoints. Their original conditions and adverse/null cells remain; none tests first-parent dependence with q preserved or establishes a scheduling benefit.
hypothesis: Replace independent first-parent requests within each suggestion by uniformly permuted systematic blocks of length equal to the inherited fresh-pool target, preserving the exact inherited prospective categorical rank probabilities and positive support while leaving every second-parent request on the original quantile law.

finding_summary.headline: Balanced first-parent use activated, but final scores fell across all three seeds
finding_summary.insights: Balanced prospective allocations transmitted into real accepted descendants and more complete breeder coverage. That exposure makes this a useful negative result: coverage and local parent-win counts are insufficient evidence of endpoint benefit for this fixed scheduler. The Child’s generating parents had lower absolute scores, so its extra local wins were measured against weaker references; more incumbent advances also came in smaller steps. The largest losses involved decoration hopping and sitagliptin, while median-2 and zaleplon task means improved. The chemistry assessment found substantial formal scaffold variety and useful aromatic, amine and carbonyl arrangements, alongside reactive bonds, strained closures and unspecified stereochemistry. Plausible alternative leading families remain limited even where graph counts are broad. Those descriptions do not establish which chemical feature caused the score loss. The fixed scheduling approach has a complete adverse result under this profile. The respective roles of changed parent sequences and their associated graph-RNG paths in producing those losses remain unresolved, as does contribution of the broader graph-evolution foundation.
finding_summary.results: The scheduler preserved the original prospective rank preference and balanced all 870 preallocated blocks. It consumed 75,411 of 139,200 records; the other 63,789 were unused. Each suggestion actually used every supported first parent, raising mean distinct first-parent coverage from 24.32 to 29.00. More accepted offspring beat their generating parents (720 versus 629), and more accepted records were later used for breeding (2,636 versus 2,401). Yet average offspring score fell from 0.385256 to 0.352623, and the average positive incumbent increment fell from 0.022510 to 0.018417. All fifteen task/seed runs completed on each side. Macro mean fell from 0.595670 to 0.553508, a paired change of -0.042161 against the required +0.002 gain. Every seed macro declined; eleven task/seed endpoints declined and four improved. The improved cells were zaleplon seeds 0 and 2 and median-2 seeds 1 and 2. Macro dispersion also decreased, from 0.026593 to 0.018224, without meeting the performance prediction.

molecular.headline: Aromatic and ring-rich molecules retain useful amines and carbonyls alongside reactive bonds, strained rings and unspecified stereochemistry
molecular.overall_character: All fifteen Child and fifteen published Parent Search trajectory paths, and all six frozen summaries, were present and read. The immutable context reports child_complete=true and paired_complete=true for seeds 0, 1 and 2; no objective or comparison is absent. Each side has 900 records per task, including 870 accepted optimizer molecules. Trajectory maxima agree with every supplied summary. This assessment describes those evaluated outputs, not unselected internal graph pools. The molecules include substituted indole carboxamides and unsaturated four-membered fused rings, linked aza-aromatic thioamides, aryl-containing aliphatic amines, bridged nitrogen/carbonyl systems, and fluorinated imino/dione heterocycles. The Child digest ring-closure incidences are 0.969, 0.9782, 0.9805, 0.9782 and 0.9678; aromatic-string incidences are 0.9655, 0.9782, 0.977, 0.9736 and 0.9621 in the fixed task order. These are molecule-level text-feature incidences, not ring counts or aromatic-atom fractions. Offline RDKit inspection gives Child median heavy-atom counts 25, 40, 32, 33 and 29, versus Parent 25, 33, 31, 30 and 27. Typed/generic Murcko graph counts among accepted optimizer outputs, counting the empty acyclic scaffold, are Child 267/112, 465/352, 365/252, 507/340 and 319/195; Parent 295/124, 404/277, 391/259, 584/406 and 208/93. Generic graphs erase atom and bond types. These counts show substantial formal graph variety, while leading molecules within individual seeds often share a much narrower chemical family. Neither distinct strings nor these scaffold counts establish plausible independent chemical coverage. Scaffold similarity, recorded founder reachability and demonstrated atom retention are separate observations. The evaluated trajectories contain no atom-mapped genealogy; this report neither reconstructs founder ancestry nor claims that recognizable initial motifs prove retained atoms. Every Child task has stereocentre-string incidence 0.0; neutral strings nevertheless contain available aliphatic amines. Questionable synthesis and weak overall drug-likeness reflect local heteroatom-halogen bonds, peroxide links and problematic ring geometry alongside familiar functional groups, not a computed feasibility score. Graph parsing and oracle labels establish neither synthesis nor stability, conformation or biological activity. The digest final excerpts are late seed-2 evaluations, not all seed incumbents. All cited_smiles below are exact task-scoped Child strings in the trusted request paths; Parent descriptions refer to its authoritative published trajectories and seed/evaluation locations. The transferable gaps preserve their historical source in n-c55c3d520a2c under its Development profile and their later baseline observation in n-62daf219c70a; historical evidence is not pooled into the current matched comparison. No chemical association here identifies mechanism activation, component contribution or an Anchor decision.

per_task.generated_character: The seed-0 leader (evaluation 256) is a 23-heavy-atom, three-ring N-brominated indole carboxamide with an N-hydroxy-N-phenyl amide. Seed 2 (279) has a 24-heavy-atom indole carboxamide with an N-amino substituent, chlorophenyl, methyl and fluoromethyl groups. Seed 1 (262) instead has 25 heavy atoms: a methoxy/vinyl-substituted benzene fused to an unsaturated four-membered carbon ring, joined through a thioamide/hydrazone group to pyridine. The three leaders therefore share aromatic surface and a polar carbonyl/thione region but do not share the same ring topology. The ordinary indole and amide motifs are recognizable synthetic starting points; the four-membered unsaturation, N-Br and N-N/O environments need separate feasibility assessment. The published Parent likewise has indole-derived amide/dicarbonyl families and an unsaturated linker family. Its seed-1 leader (293) is a pyridyl N-hydroxy carboxamide with N-F; its seed-2 leader (294) is an aryl diketone. This Child does not lack rings or aromatic groups.
liabilities: N-bromination and other N-halogen variants are distinct from ordinary carbon-bound halogens and bring local reactivity concerns.
The unsaturated four-membered fused carbon ring raises geometry and stability concerns; high score and valid aromatic notation do not resolve them.
N-amino, N-hydroxy and hydrazone derivatives require environment-specific assessment, and overgrown aromatic duplicates can have extremely low scores.
missing_features: High-scoring examples do not establish a comparably useful, geometrically credible replacement for the unsaturated four-membered ring while preserving its linker arrangement; the indole leader is an alternative topology but not an isolated replacement experiment.

Conventional local alternatives to the leading N-Br, N-O and N-N substitutions are not consistently demonstrated at the same scores. These records do not identify an exact absent target pharmacophore.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial indole anilide scores 0.3051048083696145. Child leaders for seeds 0/1/2 score 0.44024381449798056, 0.4475341963854715 and 0.4394278959350887; published Parent leaders score 0.39405142067435733, 0.47411701813450596 and 0.438972502037081. Within the seed-1 fused-ring family, the N-amino thioamide scores 0.4369542269692598; its terminal methylene-imine derivative scores 0.4475341963854715, while the chloromethylene-imine derivative scores 0.4201182934804424. These local comparisons suggest sensitivity to the polar linker and substituent pattern, not a general benefit of adding halogen. A much larger linked indole-amide structure at seed 2/evaluation 31 scores 1.7997013645006645e-14, and N=S scores 0.0. The visible reward is for a particular compact aromatic/polar organization; both fragmentation and extensive duplication can lose it. The seed-2 leader lacks an N-halogen bond, so that liability is not necessary for the observed high-score region.

per_task.generated_character: The seed-0 leader (289) has 43 heavy atoms and four six-membered aromatic rings linked by carbonyl, carbon-carbon and thioether connections, with methoxy, fluoro and tertiary aryl-amino substituents. The seed-1 leaders have 34 heavy atoms and connect a substituted pyridine to a fused nitrogen heterocycle through a thioamide; the appended oxygen-containing ring includes an O-O bond. The seed-2 leader (295) is a 39-heavy-atom, densely cross-linked O/N polycycle with ten RDKit-perceived rings, an N-O connection, exocyclic unsaturation and a chloroethyl imine substituent. Across accepted output, median size is 40 heavy atoms, versus Parent 33; the Child also emits much larger graphs. The Parent seed-0 leader (297), at 31 heavy atoms, combines linked nitrogen-rich carbonyl/thione heterocycles rather than the Child seed-2 dense polycycle. Familiar heteroaryl and thioamide pieces coexist with peroxide chemistry and challenging cross-links, so synthesis is questionable despite abundant rings.
liabilities: The seed-1 leaders contain a cyclic O-O link, which must be assessed as peroxide chemistry rather than an ordinary ether.
The seed-2 dense polycycles contain N-O connectivity and multiple constrained unsaturated ring junctions; perceived ring count does not demonstrate accessible conformation or synthesis.
Very large elaborations and floor-scoring fragments coexist with medium-sized leaders, without evidence that either extreme supplies useful structural context.
missing_features: The Child does not demonstrate reliable access to the particular compact linked heterocyclic organization seen in the stronger-scoring published Parent seed-0 family; this is a coverage observation, not proof of retained founder atoms or a component cause.

High-scoring families lack established geometrically accessible, locally stable alternatives to the peroxide and dense cross-linked arrangements. The near-scoring nonperoxide relative shows that O-O is not universally required.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial aryl-fused dione scores 0.548381482770623, the smaller oxygen-containing aromatic carbonyl structure at seed 0/evaluation 13 scores 0.5252566400521428, and methane scores 0.5. Child seed leaders score 0.6041124414367517, 0.6120582590041774 and 0.6112056392805056; published Parent leaders score 0.8561477222467935, 0.6248206599713055 and 0.6178024026512013. The Child seed-1 peroxide thioamide has several peripheral variants tied at 0.6120582590041774. A related ether-ring thioamide without O-O at evaluation 243 scores 0.6106181943884312; other substituents also differ, so this is a counterexample to a necessary peroxide rather than a measured peroxide effect. A still more elaborate seed-2 polycycle at evaluation 291 scores 0.5830654842582195. These examples associate useful scores with connected heteroaromatic/polar arrangements, but do not support more atoms or more ring closures as a sufficient improvement.

per_task.generated_character: The Child leaders combine aromatic surfaces with available aliphatic amines. Seed 2/evaluation 261 has 27 heavy atoms, two substituted benzene rings, a dimethylamino alkyl linker, methoxy and aniline groups, carbon-bound fluorine, and a three-membered carbon ring fused across adjacent aromatic atoms. Seed 0/evaluation 278 has 28 heavy atoms, a secondary ethylamino side chain and two four-membered rings in its fused aryl/amine region. Seed 1/evaluation 270 has 32 heavy atoms, a saturated diazacycle, substituted cyclopentane, phenolic/aniline groups and an O-Cl substituent. The published Parent leaders instead include a flexible tertiary diarylalkylamine (seed 0/evaluation 284), an aminoalkyl pyrrolidine/aryl ether (1/261), and a pyrrolidine-substituted fused thioether/biaryl structure (2/285). Basic centres are already represented on both sides. The general aryl-amine chemistry is recognizable, but small fused rings, reactive substituents and unspecified stereochemistry prevent calling the complete output routinely makeable.
liabilities: Three-membered fusion across aromatic atoms and fused four-membered unsaturated/amine rings raise geometry concerns in two leading seed families.
O-Cl in the seed-1 leader and N-Br in a near-leading analogue are reactive heteroatom-halogen environments, distinct from aryl C-F.
Potential stereogenic saturated centres are unassigned; substantial hydrophobic aromatic/alkyl content and halogen substitution lack measured solubility or stability evidence.
missing_features: Stereochemically specified versions of the saturated and benzylic amine arrangements are absent; no stereochemical score advantage is established by these records.

The Child does not consistently combine the favorable aryl/amine arrangement with uncomplicated ring geometry and stable peripheral bonds. The conventional Parent and other Child amine families show that strained rings are not a universal requirement.
Neutral SMILES leave protonation-state identity unresolved, but do not show a shortage of basic amine centres.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: Child seed leaders score 0.9874292093764064, 0.9784767548470228 and 0.9957754200918986; published Parent leaders score 0.9999989177995104, 0.9969753164881906 and 0.9999934235240012. A dichloroaryl sulfonate at Child seed 0/evaluation 12 scores 0.00024675866379847753 and an N-sulfonyl cyclic amine at seed 2/evaluation 40 scores 0.0009033673512242757. Together with the high aryl/aliphatic-amine scores, this associates reward with accessible amine presentation and aromatic context, not nitrogen or halogen count alone. On the same seed-2 framework, aniline scores 0.9957754200918986, N-bromoaniline 0.9933512691124673, and replacement of that amino group by bromine 0.9897931936183455. The N-Br liability is therefore not required, and even the aromatic amino group is not absolutely necessary in this local neighborhood. The seed-1 example at evaluation 254 scores 0.9675302417924879 without a three- or four-membered ring; the Parent also supplies high-scoring conventional amine families. These labels do not measure binding mode, selectivity or chemical stability.

per_task.generated_character: Seed 2/evaluation 275 has 33 heavy atoms: a fused aromatic-labelled N/O framework bearing propyl and ethoxy groups, an exocyclic alkene and an eight-membered N-methyl diaza-lactam. Its perceived rings include an oxygen-containing four-membered ring, so the lowercase aromatic labels should not be equated with a conventional furan. Seed 0/evaluation 295 is a 33-heavy-atom bridged diaryl aza/oxa carbonyl system; seed 1/evaluation 262 is a 36-heavy-atom diaryl nitrogen/dicarbonyl framework containing a ten-membered ring. The Parent similarly produces quinoline-linked or diaryl bridged nitrogen-carbonyl families, including 29- to 34-heavy-atom leaders. Carbonyl acceptors, aliphatic and aromatic nitrogens, ethers and aromatic surfaces are already abundant. The central limitation is credible connectivity and stereochemical identity, rather than a shortage of these groups. Formal typed/generic scaffold diversity is substantial, although the high-score neighborhoods recur within seed.
liabilities: An aromatic-labelled oxygen-containing four-membered ring in the seed-2 family raises a specific bond-geometry concern, beyond generic ring richness.
Bridges, exocyclic unsaturation and medium or large nitrogen rings complicate synthetic access and conformational control.
Some nearby alternatives introduce N-N connections, and potentially stereogenic saturated environments remain unspecified.
missing_features: The leading frameworks do not establish simpler, accessible connectivities retaining the same favorable aromatic/nitrogen/carbonyl organization at their exact scores; a non-four-membered alternative supplies a useful counterexample to an absolute small-ring requirement.
Stereochemical and conformational identity of saturated bridges and medium rings is unresolved. The observed labels do not isolate a benefit from resolving it.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The initial aryl-fused dione scores 0.1678386594791329; Child seed leaders score 0.21751282251166082, 0.23172955456689714 and 0.24318672855696005, versus published Parent leaders 0.2258403994203931, 0.2214095461892601 and 0.22600312875247064. The much less integrated aromatic/ester structure at Child seed 0/evaluation 25 scores 0.08310281191431669, while ethyne scores 0.0. In the seed-2 leader family, extending the exocyclic connection gives 0.24137237792276958; changing one lactam N-methyl to N-ethyl gives 0.23274735785135373. This supports a local balance of aromatic, nitrogen and carbonyl organization rather than unrestricted elaboration. An alternative at seed 2/evaluation 250 scores 0.23161309683666387 without a perceived four-membered ring, so that unusual ring is not necessary for the broader high-score region. None of these contrasts identifies a uniquely missing reference scaffold or attributes reward to a single ring-forming component.

per_task.generated_character: The seed-0 leader (228) has 26 heavy atoms: a fused N-rich imino/carbonyl heterocycle, methyl and carbon-bound fluoromethyl/fluoro substituents, and a phenolic aromatic-labelled fragment with an extra connection creating a three-membered cycle. It has no N-F bond. Seed 1/evaluation 276 has 30 heavy atoms, a fused dione, N-F and N-S connections, a substituted cyclopropene, and an aryl fluorinated formate-bearing appendage. Seed 2/evaluation 294 has 29 heavy atoms, an aromatic-labelled nine-membered nitrogen/dicarbonyl ring bearing N-F, plus a fluorinated bridged ketone/amine region. The Parent seed-2 leader (273) instead contains a small cyclic cumulene attached to a nitrogen-rich imino/carbonyl ring; its other seeds retain related fluorinated fused diones. This Child still produces difficult small-ring and aromatic-labelled geometries even when the strongest molecule lacks the Parent leader's cyclic cumulene. These are compact polar/fluorinated graphs, not established stable, stereochemically defined compounds.
liabilities: The extra bond in the phenolic fragment creates a three-membered ring within an aromatic-labelled framework, requiring geometric scrutiny.
Other seed leaders contain N-F, N-S, small unsaturated rings and densely bridged carbonyl systems; ordinary atom valence does not establish routine synthesis.
High local score sensitivity persists while the doubtful core remains present, so the labels do not certify chemical feasibility.
missing_features: Geometrically credible alternatives retaining the locally favorable fluorinated/polar organization are not established at the leading scores. The strongest Child lacking N-F is a counterexample to an obligatory reactive nitrogen-fluorine bond.
The imino/carbonyl, phenolic and large aromatic-labelled ring systems lack demonstrated tautomeric and conformational identity; stereochemical identity is also unspecified where applicable.
No exact absent target pharmacophore can be inferred from these substitution-sensitive trajectories; the evidence supports conditional chemical-context gaps.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: Child seed leaders score 0.6032522572942131, 0.37136550370722343 and 0.5193124663440728; published Parent leaders score 0.6510211907030741, 0.4870057305679067 and 0.7208853668418119. On the seed-0 leading framework, replacing N-fluoromethyl with N-hydroxy gives 0.023014746427507116, while removing the ring carbon-bound fluorine gives 0.5350327421621569. The N-F analogue with the same carbon-side fluoromethyl scores 0.48575284486531267; a further side-chain extension with N-F gives 0.5991541639620191. The local response is strongly dependent on the complete substitution pattern, and the best Child has carbon-bound fluorine rather than a necessary N-F bond. Isolated F scores 1.1043196211273875e-26, and an overgrown fused-dione assembly at seed 2/evaluation 39 scores 7.691926454927339e-16. Thus neither fluorine presence alone nor duplication of a polar heterocycle supplies the favorable molecular context. The observed local sensitivities do not establish that the strained or aromatic-labelled core is physically accessible.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Historical source: n-c55c3d520a2c, Development Search seeds 0, 1 and 2, 300 observations per task and batch size 10; re-observed in published baseline n-62daf219c70a and now n-f68f386d4d9d under the frozen Research-in-Depth epoch-1 profile. Current high-score neighborhoods contain N-Br, N-F, O-Cl and cyclic O-O connections. Counterexamples include a high-scoring carbon-fluorinated imino/carbonyl leader without N-F, an aniline scoring above its N-bromo analogue, and a near-scoring ether-ring thioamide without peroxide. The gap is local and conditional, not an absence of stable halogen chemistry or useful amines.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not consistently preserve conventional local bond environments around otherwise useful aromatic and polar frameworks.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Task-agnostic transformations need bond-environment awareness and plausible local alternatives while preserving functional relationships supported by accepted feedback. Distinguish carbon-bound halogens from heteroatom-halogen bonds and ordinary ethers from peroxides. These associations do not establish a universal filter, replacement benefit or responsible component.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Historical source: n-c55c3d520a2c, Development Search seeds 0, 1 and 2, 300 observations per task and batch size 10; re-observed in published baseline n-62daf219c70a and now n-f68f386d4d9d under the frozen Research-in-Depth epoch-1 profile. The current outputs include an unsaturated four-membered ring fused to benzene, three-membered closures across aromatic-labelled atoms, an oxygen-containing aromatic-labelled four-membered ring, and densely cross-linked heterocycles. High-scoring conventional cyclic-amine families and a non-four-membered-ring nitrogen/carbonyl alternative are counterexamples to a universal need for these geometries.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator can make many ring graphs but does not consistently supply credible geometry for small-ring unsaturation, aromatic closures and dense bridges.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Ring transformations need awareness of ring size, unsaturation, junction geometry and accessible alternative connectivity. Perceived aromaticity and formal ring counts cannot replace this information. Preserve ordinary small rings and feasible fused systems; no score gain from a blanket ring prohibition or a particular replacement is established.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Historical source: n-c55c3d520a2c, Development Search seeds 0, 1 and 2, 300 observations per task and batch size 10; re-observed in published baseline n-62daf219c70a and now n-f68f386d4d9d under the frozen Research-in-Depth epoch-1 profile. All current digest stereocentre-string incidences are 0.0, while parsed amine-bearing, fluorinated and bridged molecules contain unassigned potential tetrahedral centres. Achiral aromatic examples also occur, and neutral strings already contain available basic amines; absence of a charge marker is a separate observation.
transferable_gaps.gap: The output does not specify stereochemical identity after generating potentially stereogenic saturated and bridged centres.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Representations and transformations should preserve or resolve stereochemical identity when the generated environment requires it, while distinguishing achiral or configurationally unstable cases. Protonation and tautomerism need separate treatment. The output demonstrates unspecified identity, not an observed stereochemical score penalty or an attributed mechanism failure.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Historical source: n-c55c3d520a2c, Development Search seeds 0, 1 and 2, 300 observations per task and batch size 10; re-observed in published baseline n-62daf219c70a and now n-f68f386d4d9d under the frozen Research-in-Depth epoch-1 profile. The current trajectories contain tiny floor-scoring molecules and large low-scoring duplicated aromatic/carbonyl assemblies, including late fragments. Compact connected aromatic/polar or aryl/amine arrangements can score well, while additional cross-linking can score lower. Stronger-scoring compact Parent families and varied Child sizes rule out a general requirement for either larger or smaller graphs.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not reliably retain useful molecular context while avoiding both fragmentation and excessive structural duplication.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Task-local accepted feedback can guide transformations that preserve useful functional relationships and test simplification or replacement of dispensable regions. The missing capability is conditional control of context loss and elaboration. A fixed minimum size, size maximization, retained-founder preference or atom-retention requirement does not follow from these observations.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Historical source: n-c55c3d520a2c, Development Search seeds 0, 1 and 2, 300 observations per task and batch size 10; re-observed in published baseline n-62daf219c70a and now n-f68f386d4d9d under the frozen Research-in-Depth epoch-1 profile. Current trajectories have hundreds of distinct typed and generic Murcko graphs, but high-score neighborhoods often repeat an indole/linker, linked heteroaryl thioamide, aryl-amine or bridged nitrogen/carbonyl arrangement within seed. Other seeds and nonperoxide or non-small-ring alternatives provide genuine coverage counterexamples. This supports limited plausible leading-family alternatives, not global scaffold collapse. Structural counts do not establish founder ancestry or retained atoms.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not consistently offer chemically plausible alternative topologies within the leading local families, despite substantial formal scaffold variety.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Task-agnostic scaffold transformations can test alternative feasible connectivities that preserve learned favorable functional relationships. Evaluate their accepted outcomes rather than treating more strings, cores or recorded founders as automatically useful. Preserve source/profile boundaries; chemical similarity and descendant reachability do not establish atom conservation, mediation or component contribution.

method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.

method_references.title: Austin Tripp and José Miguel Hernández-Lobato. Genetic algorithms are strong baselines for molecule generation. arXiv:2310.09267, 2023. Sections 2–3 and Appendix A describe the anchor.

retained_mechanisms: Task-local accepted-score graph evolution and greedy score/serial survival capped at 64, with the complete chronological accepted archive retained.

Original three score-quantile band masses and positive support for prospective first-parent allocation; the evaluated variant adds B=160 systematic blocks with random permutation and actual-use accounting.
Independent inherited second-parent group/member draws with original first-partner exclusion and no-group fallback; shared task-seeded graph RNG.
Connected-fragment crossover, unchanged post-crossover mutation probability, single-atom replacement, append/delete/insert, bond change, ring opening/closing and inherited multi-step mutation walks.
Direct aromatic C/N exchange remains disabled; passive aromatic-pair enumeration and unreachable exchange code remain in the implementation.
Sanitization, stable canonical identity admission, accepted/emitted and temporary-pool duplicate checks, bounded retries and fresh surplus pools.
Integer-count Morgan features, generalized Tanimoto kernel, full real accepted-score GP fit, population-standard-deviation normalization, fixed noise/jitter and full covariance.
Correlated posterior draws, sequential availability masks, exact pool/emission/pending provenance and subsequent accepted-feedback probes.
Fresh objective-local state, announced ten-member feedback batches and protocol-owned Search seeds, oracle budgets and formal resource limits.
